text:
laura_sales: Quick sync: ACME Health prefers PrivateLink for their POC instead of VPC peering. They want minimal blast radius and only an interface endpoint in their app VPC. Can we draft a minimal ask list and steps to hand off? @mike_solutions @dinesh_neteng
mike_solutions: Short checklist from infra side: we create a VPCE service in our infra account fronted by an NLB. Customer creates an Interface VPCE (ENI) in their subnet to the service. What we need from them: subnet IDs, target subnets for the ENIs, the security admin contact, and whether they want Private DNS enabled. No TGW route changes required solely for interface endpoints.
dinesh_neteng: Networking notes to include for the customer: - Their chosen subnets must have free IPs for the VPCE ENIs. - Ensure their app SG allows outbound to the VPCE ENI. - Our NLB SG must permit inbound 443 from their VPCE ENI CIDRs or the app SG. - VPCE traffic uses the ENI path, so they don't need to touch route tables except to ensure egress still goes to NAT/IGW for outside access. - If they expect on-prem traffic via Direct Connect -> TGW to reach the VPCE ENIs, share the on-prem CIDR ranges so we can adjust allowlists.

Sample security group snippet we can send them:
```
Type: HTTPS (TCP 443)
Source: vpce-eni-cidr OR sg-<their-app-sg>
Description: allow PrivateLink traffic to Redwood NLB
```

Also note: NLB targets are IPs (or instances). If they use instance targets and rely on instance IPs, they may need to disable source/dest checks on those instances. For our typical NLB -> IP target flow no extra route edits are required.
irene_security: Security/business requirements to ask ACME (short): - Enable VPC Flow Logs for the app VPC (retain at least 30 days). - Share CloudTrail entries for VPCE creation/events during the POC window. - Confirm log retention/compliance tags, especially if any PII touches logs. - If they want mTLS, note that we can support it but it requires customer-provided certs and a brief config in the SOW. Add that as an opt-in item.
mike_solutions: DNS options to present: Option A (recommended): Customer enables Private DNS on the Interface VPCE. That makes our api hostname resolve to the VPCE address automatically inside their VPC. Option B: Customer creates a private hosted zone and CNAME to the VPCE endpoint DNS name if they prefer explicit control.

Quick validation steps we run from their side after VPCE creation (share with customer):
```
# run from an instance in the app subnet
dig +short api.redwood-inference.internal @169.254.169.253
curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.internal/health --resolve "api.redwood-inference.internal:443:<vpce-eni-ip>"
```

laura_sales: Great. I'll ask ACME for: subnet IDs, sg admin contact, whether they want Private DNS, and on-prem CIDRs if applicable. They want the POC in ~2 weeks. infra-bot: can you provision the provisional NLB + test service in sandbox once we have the subnets? :thumbsup:
infra-bot: infra-bot created a provisional NLB + test backend in sandbox (nlb-sbx-0a1b2c3d) at 1850012380 and will hold the service until we have real VPCE details.
mike_solutions: After laura shares the subnets and DNS preference, I'll provide the service name (com.amazonaws.vpce.<region>.vpce-svc-xxxx) and the NLB ARN, and flag whether we need a cert thumbprint for mTLS.
irene_security: I'll attach the short security checklist to the email as well (VPC Flow Logs, CloudTrail, SG allowlist, mTLS opt-in) and ask their security contact for an acknowledgement.

laura_sales: I'll draft the handoff email now with the checklist, sample SG rule, and the dig/curl steps. Thanks all, I'll update when I have their subnet IDs. :grinning:
